tayla: Hey team — customer reported a sudden burst of 429s right after we failed their traffic from us-east-1 -> eu-west-1. They say the app was healthy but when our routing kicked in they saw a flood of rate_limit_exceeded. Sample log lines below. Can eng-sre confirm whether cross-region throttles or per-region quotas could cause this?

anya: Can you paste the exact request_id(s) and the X-Region/X-Routing headers? Need to know if this was a fanout (duplicated requests) or a single redirected request. Also, did they have any Dedicated capacity in eu-west?

tayla: Request IDs: req_202401213_abc, req_202401213_def. Logs:```
[2024-01-21T14:02:09Z] req=req_202401213_abc region=eu-west-1 status=429 reason=rate_limit_exceeded route=cross-region/fanout rps=248
[2024-01-21T14:02:09Z] req=req_202401213_def region=eu-west-1 status=429 reason=rate_limit_exceeded route=cross-region/fanout rps=260
```Headers we see on our side: `X-Client-Region: us-east-1`, `X-Routed-To: eu-west-1`. Customer says baseline RPS was ~140, then they launched a batch job which spiked to ~300 and we triggered failover.

sam: Quick note: our failover policy for that customer is `fanout_then_pick` for short windows (we attempt both primary+secondary then pick fastest). If the secondary already has non-trivial load, the aggregate can exceed per-region customer throttle. There is a per-customer per-region soft cap (200 rps) + a short-term burst window. Looks like they hit the soft cap after fanout.

anya: Steps to reproduce (from our side) that we'll run: 1) Replay their load (140 rps steady + 160 rps burst) from us-east to trigger failover. 2) Enable routing debug and capture `route_decision` traces. 3) Check `capacity_pool` usage for eu-west-1 for that tenant.

tayla: Repro steps I already ran from a sandbox:```
# quick load repro (sandbox)
for i in {1..300}; do \n  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" -H "X-Client-Region: us-east-1" \\n    -d '{"prompt":"hi","max_tokens":1}' https://api.redwood.local/v1/generate &\ndone\nwait\n```I saw the same 429 pattern with `route=cross-region/fanout` in the debug logs.

ops-bot: Alert: capacity_pool eu-west-1 at 86% for tenant=acme-corp during 2024-01-21T14:00-14:05Z. Autoscale policy hit max_burst.

anya: Likely root cause: fanout + existing region utilization pushed tenant above per-region throttle -> 429s. Remediation options: - temporarily increase tenant reserved capacity in eu-west-1 - change failover policy to `sticky_prefer_primary` or `sequential_failover` (avoid simultaneous fanout) - advise customer to stagger their batch job or limit burst.

billing-bot: FYI — bumping reserved capacity will increase monthly committed billing. Temporary bump can be PR-approved by infra on-call.

sam: I can apply a short-lived routing policy change (10m) to switch that customer's failover to sequential and monitor. Anya, can you confirm which exact policy name to push?

anya: Use `sequential_failover_v2` (it tries secondary only after primary fails for 2s, avoids immediate fanout). If ops approves, I'll push policy and add a canary flag. I'll also open a capacity ticket to Capacity team to review eu-west headroom and advise on long-term reserved capacity.

tayla: Thanks — please push the policy and let me know when done so I can inform the customer and provide repro notes. Also capturing the customer-visible guidance: "If you expect short-lived large bursts, request a temporary regional capacity increase or switch to sequential failover to avoid cross-region throttles."

anya: Will do. I'll update this thread with the routing trace and ticket link once created.

sam: Policy change applied to tenant=acme-corp: `sequential_failover_v2` (rolled for 10m). Monitoring now.

tayla: Confirmed customer reports error rate dropping to baseline after change. Closing for now — will reopen if we see recurrence. :tada:
